Look for terms like "rate limit", "rateLimit", "throttle", "RateLimiter", "express-rate-limit", "rate_limit", middleware registration files, etc. across the whole codebase (backend/server code, not just frontend).

Report back:
1. Whether any rate-limiting middleware exists at all in this repo.
2. If it exists, exact file path(s) where it's defined and where it's registered/wired into the app (e.g., app.use(...) call site), with line numbers.
3. What the actual configured limits are (requests per window, per user vs per IP, etc.) — quote the exact config values.
4. If nothing like this exists, say so clearly and note what related things DO exist (e.g., any throttling, debouncing, or unrelated "limit" usages) so I can give an accurate premise-correction answer.

Be thorough — check multiple naming conventions and search broadly before concluding it doesn't exist.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

This confirms it: `imageProcessingSemaphore` is a global concurrency limiter (max 2 concurrent EXIF-stripping operations across all users), not a per-user rate limit and not time-window based.

I now have a complete picture. Here's my report.

## Findings

**1. Does per-user API rate-limiting middleware exist? NO.**

I searched the entire repository (this is the `usememos/memos` Go backend + React frontend) for `rate limit`, `rateLimit`, `rate_limit`, `RateLimiter`, `throttle`, `express-rate-limit`, `x/time/rate`, `429`/`TooManyRequests`, and middleware/interceptor registration sites. There is no rate-limiting middleware anywhere in the codebase — backend or frontend.

**2/3. Nothing to report** — no file defines it, no `app.use(...)`/interceptor chain registers it, and there are no configured limit values, because it doesn't exist.

**4. What actually exists (for an accurate premise-correction answer):**

- **No HTTP-layer rate limiting at all.** The middleware/interceptor stack is fully enumerated at:
  - `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:51-52` — Echo server only registers `middleware.Recover()` and a CORS middleware (`newCORSMiddleware`), nothing else.
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-141` — the Connect-RPC interceptor chain: `NewMetadataInterceptor()`, `NewLoggingInterceptor()`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor()`, `NewAuthInterceptor()`. All four are defined in `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`. None throttle requests — they handle header propagation, logging, panic recovery, and auth only.
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69-97` — a `gatewayAuthMiddleware` wraps the gRPC-Gateway mux, again auth-only, no rate limiting.

- **Two concurrency semaphores exist, but these are NOT rate limiters** (no time window, not per-user, global across all users):
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59` — `thumbnailSemaphore: semaphore.NewWeighted(3)` — limits to 3 concurrent thumbnail generations.
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:60` — `imageProcessingSemaphore: semaphore.NewWeighted(2)` — limits to 2 concurrent EXIF-stripping operations.
  - Used at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_image.go:67-75` (`acquireImageProcessingSlot`) and consumed at `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:158-160`, which returns `codes.ResourceExhausted, "too many image processing requests"` when the semaphore can't be acquired. This is a global in-flight-request cap, not a per-user or per-IP rate limit.

- `golang.org/x/time v0.15.0` appears in `go.mod:151` but only as an **indirect** (transitive) dependency — the `x/time/rate` package is never imported/used anywhere in the Go source (confirmed via grep for `golang.org/x/time/rate` across all `.go` files: zero matches). So even the standard Go rate-limiting library isn't actually wired up.

- Other unrelated "limit"/"too many" occurrences found are just batch-size validation guards (business logic, not rate limiting), e.g.:
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/instance_service.go:78` — max batch get instance settings
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service.go:145` — max batch get usernames
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:355` — max batch delete attachments
  - `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_link_metadata.go:24` — max batch get link metadata
  - `/bench/home/work/store/attachment.go:97` — default page-size limit for loading attachments

- `/bench/home/work/internal/email/doc.go:86` contains only a **documentation comment/TODO**: `- Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse` — this is an aspirational note in a doc comment, not an implementation. No corresponding code exists.

- On the frontend (`web/src`), the only related hits are unrelated UI debouncing utilities: `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useDebouncedEffect.ts` and its usages in `MemoEditor` components (`useLinkMemo.ts`, `cacheService.ts`, `InsertMenu.tsx`) — these debounce local UI effects/autosave, not API request throttling, and are client-side only.

**Bottom line:** This repository has no per-user (or per-IP) API rate-limiting middleware. The closest things are (a) a documentation TODO mentioning email rate limiting that was never implemented, and (b) two small global concurrency semaphores (limits of 3 and 2 concurrent operations) guarding thumbnail/image-processing work, which cap simultaneous in-flight operations server-wide rather than limiting requests per user over a time window.
